title: Ahalya Was Never Stone
source: Valmiki Ramayana, Bala Kanda 1(47-48) (Critical Edition; vulgate 1.48-49)

captions.instagram:
Did a stone really turn into a woman at the touch of Rama's foot?

We grew up hearing that Ahalya was a stone until Rama's foot touched her. Valmiki's Ramayana tells it differently: she lived unseen in the hermitage, on air, in penance — and when Rama came, it was Rama and Lakshmana who touched HER feet.

📜 Source: Valmiki Ramayana, Bala Kanda 1(47-48) (Critical Edition; vulgate 1.48-49)

captions.youtube_description:
Did a stone really turn into a woman at the touch of Rama's foot?

We grew up hearing that Ahalya was a stone until Rama's foot touched her. Valmiki's Ramayana tells it differently: she lived unseen in the hermitage, on air, in penance — and when Rama came, it was Rama and Lakshmana who touched HER feet.

Source: Valmiki Ramayana, Bala Kanda 1(47-48) (Critical Edition; vulgate 1.48-49)
Verses:
• Gautama's curse: she will live in the hermitage on air, without food, in penance, sleeping on ashes, invisible to all beings — no stone — 1.47.29
• She will be purified when Rama, son of Dasharatha, comes to this forest — 1.47.30
• When Rama arrives she is seen radiant, like the full moon veiled by smoke / frost and cloud — 1.48.14-15
• Rama and Lakshmana took hold of (touched) Ahalya's feet; remembering Gautama's words she received them — 1.48.17
• She offered padya, arghya and hospitality; Rama accepted — 1.48.18
• A great rain of flowers fell, with the sound of divine drums — 1.48.19
• The stone (petrification) version is a later development: credited first to Kalidasa's Raghuvamsha, then Puranas, Kamban, Adhyatma Ramayana, Ramcharitmanas — absent from Valmiki CE 1.47-48
